segments.t: Shares of Kupang are set to begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange today.
The South Korean e-commerce giant, oftentimes compared to Amazon,
just completed the largest IPO by an Asian company on a U.S. exchange since Alibaba in 2014.
Kupang priced its IPO with $35 a share. That's above the target range.
It gives the company a market value of $60 billion.
Joining us right now first on CNBC is Kupang's founder and CEO, Kupang Kim.
It's great to see you, Bob. The last time we saw each other was in Seoul.
And here you are in New York. It's been quite a ride.
The former private valuation, I think, is now up six times since effectively we last spoke.
Let's talk about this company. For those who are uninitiated, we just referenced Amazon.
But it really is Amazon, DoorDash, Instacart, all-in-one in South Korea.
And it's a company I've talked a lot about. We've had you on the show before.
Lots of companies have been trying to buy you for years. So here you are, independent and
continuing on. Talk to us about the path to profitability, if you could this morning,
because you've been growing wildly on the revenue side and the losses have come down.
But what does it look like over the next couple of years?
I think we've been fortunate to be working with all my colleagues and investors who've been aligned
and unwavering on the long-term strategy. We're here because we've kept our eyes on that long-term
strategy to build real value for our customers and our shareholders. So I think we will continue
to remain focused. This IPO now gives us resources to remain steadfast on that journey. So we're
really, really excited. So what are you going to do with the money? We're going to continue
to invest in innovations like Dawn Delivery and continue to invest in the regional economies
throughout Korea, create great jobs, continue to invest in the technology and end-to-end
integration. Dawn Delivery, for example, Andrew, you might remember.
